title.narrative: GLA 2 - Ghana

description.narrative: The Green Livelihood Alliance Ghana is a partnership among Tropenbos Ghana, A Rocha Ghana andFriends of the Earth Ghana (FoE Gh) that was formed 5 years ago. It aims to continue to mobilize LocalCommunity (LC) and Civil Society campaigns, capacity strengthening, and advocacy based on empirical evidence to create a social movement that defends forests and biodiversity, and supports communities to protect their environmental rights that reduce the drivers of deforestation. The program will campaign for climate justice, execute non-violent direct actions and participate in Ghanaian, regional and international movements that implement dialogue and dissent strategies towards local communities, public and private actors. We will achieve this by mobilising people and bringing together the knowledge needed to address complex governance issues for climate-smart landscapes through a landscape approach involving local communities, private, public and civil society actors. The forested landscapes in Ghana selected for the GLA 2021 – 2025 intervention are the Atewa Forest Landscape in the Eastern Region and the Juaboso-Bia Sefwi- iawso Forest Landscape in the Western North Region.

description.narrative: Measures the advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs, for, by or with their membership/constituency at national and international level

comment.narrative: At the beginning of the GLA2 programme no CSO has yet increased L&A capcities as a result of the programme.

CSOs succeeded in creating space for CSO demandsand positions through agenda setting, influencing the debateand/or creating space to engage at national and international level 5 times. For example: Discussion in media and multi-stakeholder platforms on illegal logging in forest and off-reserves raised awareness among local communities and responsible authorities on the need for ensuring sustainable and inclusive governance of forests.

No 1st ring youth led CSO partners are expected to increase their capacity over the course of the GLA2 programme in Cameroon. No 2nd ring youth led CSO partners have been included in this target value, as the GLA is a flexible adaptable program this can't be well estimated in advance.

1 governmental policy was better implemented for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement at midline. After awareness raising and capacity building of six (6) local communities in 2021 in the use of mobile technology in forest monitoring, local forest monitors have intensified their efforts in forest monitoring and reporting in the Bia Landscape from zero to eight (8) alerts in December 2021.
